kernelIdea: f⁻¹ commutes with complement, union, and intersection. The pivot in every proof is x ∈ f⁻¹(U) ⇔ f(x) ∈ U.

kernels.l1: Trace back from two cubbies at once and you get the two groups of children put together.
kernels.l2: If you trace back from two arrowheads together, you get the same children as tracing back from each one and joining the answers.
kernels.l3: Tracing back respects the hoops: the pre-image of a union is the union of the pre-images, and the same holds for intersections and for outsides.
kernels.l4: Tracing back respects union, intersection and complement exactly. Every proof pivots on one fact: an input lies in the traced-back set exactly when its output lies in the target.
kernels.l5: Tracing back commutes with union, intersection and complement, and each proof reduces to one pivot: an input lies in the traced-back set exactly when its output lies in the target.
kernels.l6: Tracing back carries union, intersection and complement across unchanged; going forwards carries only union. That asymmetry, and the reason for it, is the content of the module.
kernels.l7: Tracing back commutes with union, intersection and complement, each proof turning on a single equivalence. Going forwards commutes only with union.
kernels.l8: f⁻¹ is a Boolean algebra homomorphism P(T) → P(S) and sits between the two image operators as an adjoint; this is why continuity is stated with pre-images.

kernel: f⁻¹(Ū) = f⁻¹(U)‾, f⁻¹(U ∪ V) = f⁻¹(U) ∪ f⁻¹(V), and f⁻¹(U ∩ V) = f⁻¹(U) ∩ f⁻¹(V). The pivot in every proof is x ∈ f⁻¹(U) ⇔ f(x) ∈ U.
objectives: Prove one of the three identities by double inclusion
namedMove: take any one and follow it
